summary: The np.where rewrite correctly eliminates the NumPy 1.24 out-of-bound-integer deprecation warnings by building a new, type-promoted array instead of forcing 256/257/258 into a uint8 array in place, while preserving the over-before-under ordering and even fixing a latent uint8 wraparound. Mergeable; only a modest memory/perf consideration is worth noting.

issues.description: np.where allocates three new full-size arrays and rewrites every element each call, whereas the original in-place fancy-index assignment only touched the (usually few) out-of-range/bad entries. On large image arrays in this hot colormap path this adds avoidable allocation/copy overhead, though it is acceptable and not blocking.

For integer (e.g. uint8) input, xa is now widened to a larger int dtype via type promotion instead of staying uint8. Downstream uses xa only as an index into self._lut (lut.take/indexing), which is dtype-agnostic, so this is harmless and arguably more correct (avoids the old 257->1 wraparound), but it is a behavior change worth being aware of.
